title: Composition of the earth's atmosphere
competency: Describe the gases of the atmosphere.

keywords.def: The envelope of air (gases) that surrounds the earth.
The gases, dust particles and moisture droplets of the atmosphere taken together.

en.text: The atmosphere is the envelope of air around the earth. It has gases, dust and water droplets, together called aerosols. Nitrogen (78%) and oxygen (21%) are the major gases; argon and carbon dioxide are minor; the rest are trace gases. Oxygen is the most important for life.

am.text: ከባቢ አየር ምድርን የከበበ አየር ነው። ናይትሮጅን (78%) እና ኦክስጅን (21%) ዋና ጋዞች ናቸው።

screens.title: Most of the air
screens.ask: Which gas makes up most of the air you breathe?
screens.after: Nitrogen: 78%. Oxygen is only 21%, but it is the one we need to live.

screens.title: The atmosphere
paras: The air that surrounds the earth is called the atmosphere.
It is transparent, colourless, tasteless and odourless.
It has gases, dust particles and moisture droplets, together called aerosols.

screens.title: Figure 1.8: the gases
paras: Nitrogen and oxygen are major gases. Argon and carbon dioxide are minor gases. The rest are trace gases.
screens.note: Nitrogen comes from volcanoes and decaying plants and animals. Oxygen is mainly produced by plants.
